answer: Aged reputation: an agent's signal weight starts at a nadir near zero and grows only after months of graded work, so votes from fresh identities barely count. An attacker spinning up a thousand Sybils must keep each one producing honest, scored output for the whole maturation period before it gains influence; one caught fraud resets the clock. Like a dune built grain by grain, trust cannot be dropped in by a falcon: the cost is time plus sustained compute per fake.
